query: Dedicated global existence verification and separate temporal RoI refinement for Soccer-GMR
platform: ResearchPilot Tier 1 APIs + primary-source retrieval + independent citation review

papers.title: Retrieving Any Relevant Moments: Benchmark and Models for Generalized Moment Retrieval
claims: Ding et al. study retrieval of all relevant intervals or an empty set, introduce Soccer-GMR, and attach an existence branch using max-pooling and a two-layer MLP over cross-modal localization representations.
limitations: Do not imply first introduction of no-target/multiple-target temporal retrieval; Qin et al. precedes this work.
Presence consumes cross-modal embeddings, not explicitly predicted temporal coordinates.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata

papers.title: Improving Target Presence and Plurality Recognition for Generalized Referring Image Segmentation
claims: Kim, Lee, and Kwak introduce a target query that reads intermediate pixel-decoder features for presence recognition, a plurality classification objective, and synthetic no- and multi-target training examples in generalized referring image segmentation.
limitations: Specify intermediate pixel-decoder features for presence; plurality is supervised from text-conditioned query features.
Evidence concerns image segmentation, not temporal retrieval.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary publisher full text, publisher metadata, and Crossref API

papers.title: QVHighlights: Detecting Moments and Highlights in Videos via Natural Language Queries
claims: QVHighlights introduces Moment-DETR for query-conditioned moment localization and highlight detection, including retrieval of multiple disjoint moments.
limitations: QVHighlights already includes multiple disjoint moments per query; do not characterize every earlier benchmark as strictly single-moment.
Its evaluation does not establish empty-set rejection.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata

papers.title: Query-Dependent Video Representation for Moment Retrieval and Highlight Detection
claims: QD-DETR builds query-dependent video representations with cross-attention and negative-pair saliency training. These evaluations do not by themselves establish no-target GMR rejection.
limitations: QD-DETR explicitly uses irrelevant video-query pairs with low-saliency supervision; avoid saying it has no negative-query training.
Original evaluation uses retrieval/highlight metrics, not a GMR empty-set rejection protocol.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary full text, arXiv metadata, and CVF proceedings

papers.title: Correlation-Guided Query-Dependency Calibration for Video Temporal Grounding
claims: CG-DETR calibrates cross-modal query dependence using adaptive attention with dummy tokens and clip-word correlation guidance. Its reported grounding/highlight evaluations do not establish GMR empty-set rejection.
limitations: Latest retrieved version is v4, July 2024; 2023 denotes first preprint.
No publication venue was verified; do not invent one.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata

papers.title: Knowing Where to Focus: Event-aware Transformer for Video Grounding
claims: EaTR uses event-aware dynamic moment queries informed by input-specific content and position.
limitations: Evaluation uses standard grounding datasets and recall/mAP; no-target rejection cannot be inferred from these results.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata

papers.title: FlashVTG: Feature Layering and Adaptive Score Handling Network for Video Temporal Grounding
claims: FlashVTG uses temporal feature layering across multiple scales and adaptive score refinement for grounding and highlight detection.
limitations: Use 2025 when citing the WACV conference version; 2024 is the preprint year.
Its TFL replaces the traditional decoder; original metrics do not establish no-target rejection.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary full text, arXiv metadata, and CVF proceedings

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
claims: LoRA freezes pretrained weights and learns low-rank update matrices. Actual runtime, memory, and inference savings for this implementation require direct measurement.
limitations: Original language-model efficiency findings are not measurements of this repository.
No repository runtime or memory result was inspected in this independent pass.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata

papers.title: CVA: Context-aware Video-text Alignment for Video Temporal Grounding
claims: CVA introduces Query-aware Context Diversification, motivating query-conditioned background replacement. Attribute only this augmentation inspiration unless the implementation also adopts CVA’s encoder or boundary loss.
limitations: QCD selects background replacements using query relevance and preserves the ground-truth moment with adjacent context.
Whether this repository implements only the inspired replacement and excludes CBD/CTE was not inspected.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary full text and arXiv metadata

papers.title: Generalized Video Moment Retrieval
claims: Qin et al. previously formulate Generalized Video Moment Retrieval with no-target and one-to-many queries, introduce NExT-VMR, and propose BCANet. Any present novelty must concern the specific method, benchmark, protocol, or measured behavior rather than first enabling these query types.
limitations: OpenReview direct access triggered browser verification; official ICLR PDF retrieved successfully.
Official PDF names the fifth author Shawn Li; secondary indexing may show Li Li.
No DOI was found in retrieved primary material.
No-target and one-to-many temporal retrieval, a corresponding dataset (NExT-VMR), and BCANet predate Ding et al. 2026.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.

papers.title: Moment of Untruth: Dealing with Negative Queries in Video Moment Retrieval
claims: Flanagan, Damen, and Wray introduce Negative-Aware Video Moment Retrieval, distinguishing in-domain and out-of-domain negatives, and evaluate retrieval and rejection on augmented QVHighlights and Charades-STA benchmarks.
limitations: Negative queries mean video-irrelevant queries, not necessarily linguistic negation.
This prior limits claims that negative-query rejection itself is novel.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary arXiv abstract and CVF publisher abstract/metadata

papers.title: Not All Inputs Are Valid: Towards Open-Set Video Moment Retrieval using Language
claims: Fang et al. study Open-Set Video Moment Retrieval and propose OpenVMR to reject video-irrelevant queries before localizing moments for relevant queries.
limitations: ACM page returned HTTP 403; Crossref confirms publisher bibliographic metadata.
Cite ACM MM 2024, not 2026, when discussing chronology.
Paper defines OOD as video-irrelevant queries; do not equate this automatically with Flanagan’s out-of-domain-negative category.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary arXiv abstract and publisher-deposited Crossref metadata
evidence_locations: arXiv abstract and author publication comment

papers.title: When One Moment Isn't Enough: Multi-Moment Retrieval with Cross-Moment Interactions
claims: Cao et al. introduce QV-M² and FlashMMR for multi-moment retrieval; its Multi-moment Post-verification module adjusts boundaries, re-evaluates candidates, and prunes low-confidence proposals.
limitations: The named module is Multi-moment Post-verification; generic cross-moment verification is acceptable but less precise.
Abstract supports multiple-moment retrieval, not an empty-set rejection claim.
papers.notes: Accepted for the limited literature claim in the independent review; not evidence for repository results.
papers.evidence_level: Primary arXiv abstract and author metadata

summary: Focused evidence pool; not a systematic review or novelty proof.
gaps: Does dedicated global querying improve rejection at matched positive recall and matched negative recall?
Which gains remain under matched optimization budgets, Val selectors and multiple seeds?
Does Gaussian pooling outperform uniform pooling in this same active configuration?
How much full-Test discrimination reflects source association versus within-WorldCup event verification?
Can positive/multi-target end-to-end recall improve without sacrificing rejection?
How do this operation and its full design differ from previous Gaussian temporal weighting/refinement methods?
What are measured adaptation cost, inference latency, memory and FLOPs?
